entries.task_id: pichi|is|an offshoot of krio
entries.description: Pichi is an offshoot of Krio
entries.subject: Pichi

spans.text: Pichi is an offshoot of Krio, which first arrived in Bioko, the former Fernando Po, with African settlers from Freetown, Sierra Leone in 1827 (Fyfe 1962: 165).

entries.description: manual labour was provided by Southern Nigerian
entries.subject: manual labour

spans.text: The bulk of manual labour was provided by Southern Nigerian, and to a lesser extent, Liberian, Ghanaian and Cameroonian contract workers, who outnumbered the Bube and Fernandino population of Bioko by the 1950s.

entries.task_id: the language|has|essentially guarded its krio character
entries.description: the language has essentially guarded its Krio character
entries.subject: the language

spans.text: Although the language has essentially guarded its Krio character, the continuous presence in Bioko of speakers of other varieties of West African Creole and Pidgin Englishes throughout the last hundred and fifty years as well as language shift from Bube (Northwest Bantu) have not gone unnoticed in the phonology, lexicon and grammar of Pichi.

spans.text: It remains to be seen how Pichi will adapt to the profound changes that Equatorial Guinea is going through at this moment.
